assessment.rationale: No open or discoverable solution provides midwife-led care for all of roughly 130,000,000 births a year, so the Main KPI is not met. An ICM-led study (January 2026) estimates the world is short about 980,000 midwives and projects a shortfall of 690,000 to 830,000 by 2030, over 90% in low- and middle-income countries (https://internationalmidwives.org/pressrelease/world-faces-shortage-of-nearly-one-million-midwives/). Even skilled attendance of any kind reached 86% of births in 2023, with 69% for the poorest fifth (https://data.unicef.org/topic/maternal-health/delivery-care/). Midwife-led systems are proven at national scale only in a few high-income countries: about 80-90% of New Zealand pregnancies register with a midwife lead maternity carer (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5038958), and the evidence base for midwife continuity is mature (Cochrane review, https://www.cochrane.org/news/cochrane-making-difference-midwifery). Honest limit: the care model itself is known and evidenced; the unsolved part is workforce, training and financing at global scale, and tasks that re-derive the clinical evidence for midwife-led care are not new work.

additionalSearches.query: State of the World's Midwifery 2025 report shortage of midwives births attended
additionalSearches.finding: ICM-led study (January 2026): about 980,000 more midwives needed across 181 countries; shortage projected at 690,000-830,000 by 2030. Africa holds nearly half the gap.

additionalSearches.query: midwife-led continuity of care models Cochrane review coverage proportion of births worldwide
additionalSearches.finding: Cochrane review (2024 update, 17 RCTs) supports midwife continuity of care; no global coverage figure exists; Australia estimated at 3-5% continuity versus about 80% in New Zealand.

additionalSearches.query: skilled birth attendance global coverage 2025 UNICEF percentage births attended by skilled health personnel
additionalSearches.finding: 86% of births had any skilled attendant in 2023 (96% richest vs 69% poorest fifth); midwife-led care specifically is far lower. Goal not met.

additionalSearches.query: Netherlands New Zealand midwife-led maternity system percentage of births lead maternity carer midwife
additionalSearches.finding: New Zealand: 91.5% of pregnancies in a national cohort registered with a midwife lead maternity carer. Midwife-led systems exist nationally only in a few countries such as New Zealand and the Netherlands.
